title: Ongoing fasts can be awarded as completed milestones
reasoning: The query filters `days__date__lt=today` before annotating `end_date=Max('days__date')`, so the aggregate only sees past days. A fast that is currently ongoing or has future days but started before today will have a computed `end_date` from its latest past day and pass `end_date__lt=today`, causing `first_nonweekly_fast_complete` to be awarded before the fast has actually ended.
recommendation: Annotate the maximum date across all fast days first, then filter on that aggregate being less than today. Avoid narrowing the joined `days` relation to past dates before calculating the max end date.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were included for these management commands, and the excerpt does not show coverage for ongoing multi-day fasts with both past and future days.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create a user participating in a non-weekly fast with one day before today and one day after today, run `award_first_nonweekly_complete_milestones`, and assert no `first_nonweekly_fast_complete` milestone is created until after the max fast day is before today.
minimumFixScope: Change the completed-fast queryset in `award_first_nonweekly_complete_milestones` so the `Max('days__date')` aggregate is computed over all days for each fast before filtering completed fasts.
